b: The Go-Betweens' Robert Forster has a novel out – it joins a wretched parade of books by pop musicians hellbent on parlaying their fame in the publishing world

Earlier this year, Robert Forster, ex-Go-Between and respected elder-statesman of indie rock, did something only a handful of his peers have had the nerve – or foolhardiness – to do before. He put his reputation on the line, flung all caution to the wind and went and published a novel. In doing so he joined a coterie of A-listers who, at some point in their careers, decided to apply their considerable talents as songwriters to longform prose fiction: a not-too-shabby crew that includes the likes of Bob Dylan, Gil Scott-Heron, Robert Calvert, Nick Cave,...
